statusText: Green - the full 24-hour window sits inside the CME weekend halt, with Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt and no price path can form. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always. The scheduled 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen falls about thirteen hours beyond the final slot in this window.
headline: A 3.75%-4.00% policy rate, a 10-year at the 5% threshold and $100 crude wait out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt: cash trading ended at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini stopped printing near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly thirteen hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's verified marks stand unchanged and were re-confirmed at primary sources this hour. Cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing within four points of the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 daily range. Friday was a quadruple-witching expiry alongside the quarterly index rebalance, and it cleared without disorder; the closing strength carried substantial mechanical flow rather than persistent momentum, which is why it is not read as one-way structure. The week's anchor was Wednesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 vote raising the target range 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00%, the first increase in more than three years, with a dot plot pointing to at least one further hike this year. Equities absorbed it and then rose into rising long-end yields rather than falling ones; the 10-year closed Friday near the 5% threshold, up about five basis points, while H.15 for 17 September shows the 2-year at 4.67% and the 10-year at 4.94%. Energy is the largest unresolved file across this weekend. Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, its principal bypass around the blocked Strait of Hormuz and a route carrying roughly 4-5% of world supply, has been shut since 11 September after a drone strike launched from Iraq, and Aramco has told European refiners they will receive no crude next month under long-term agreements. Crude nonetheless fell for a third consecutive session on Friday, WTI settling at $100.30, down about 1.6%, and Brent at $103.87, as reporting that part of the pipeline's flows could be restored outweighed fresh regional strikes; repair guidance remains conflicting, spanning days to six-to-eight weeks. A supply file being reassessed downward argues against a gap-and-extend reopen, while the conflict itself stays a live discontinuity channel: Houthi forces accused Saudi Arabia of 26 strikes in 24 hours on 18 September, and the Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb corridors remain unresolved, with the Iran-Gulf meeting on an Omani reopening plan postponed indefinitely. Friday's internals were dispersed rather than aligned: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.78% on memory names while capital rotated out of parts of mega-cap technology, and over the week the Nasdaq gained about 0.4% while the S&P 500 and the Dow posted losses, the Dow shedding more than 1.5%. The AI policy file remains the newest amplifier candidate, with AI chips and export controls on the agenda of the 24 September Trump-Xi meeting in Washington, where published analysis sets low expectations for progress; that event sits five days beyond this window. Shared cross-asset context was only partially collected this cycle, with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so no part of this assessment rests on it and every figure here was verified independently. Tail is held at its structural weekend floor because the pathological no-retracement structure it measures has no venue in which to develop. Stress is modest and drifts higher only as the stock of untested headlines grows against static marks, and Confidence decays as Friday's evidence ages. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the Sunday reopen.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-18 through the European morning and the dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell to 11, 7, 6 and 5 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final ten hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, reaching 21 across the final five slots. Confidence held between 77 and 88 throughout, drifting lower only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode rotated from trend-up in the European morning to mixed across the dispersed U.S. session, back briefly to trend-up into the close, then to normal for every hour of the weekend halt.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about thirteen hours after the final slot here. Tail is held between 5 and 7 across the window, lifting one point late on Saturday and once more early on Sunday as the reopen moves inside the horizon's edge; that drift reflects proximity and the growing stock of untested headlines - principally the Saudi pipeline and Hormuz supply file, the rates path after a hike that left the 10-year at the 5% threshold, and AI policy into the 24 September Trump-Xi meeting - rather than any observed structure. Stress rises gradually from 22 to 31 on the same reasoning, crossing into the moderate band during Saturday afternoon in New York, and Confidence decays from 76 to 65 as Friday's verified marks age without a refreshing observation. Dominant mode is normal in every slot and the mapped policy state is unchanged throughout. The genuine sensitivity of this assessment sits beyond its final hour, at the reopen, where a gap that extends without a meaningful retracement alongside aligned yields, crude and semiconductors would be the structure that matters; a gap that is absorbed and retraced would be ordinary.
